chunkSummary: Lines 5092-6277: the bulk-actions UI layer (recent, 2026, already ES2020+, no jQuery). Two classes - BulkActionModal (basket modal DOM, 301 lines) and BulkActionGridController (grid <-> basket <-> runner wiring, 697 lines) - plus ensureBulkActionCheckboxes (KTL checkbox wiring), bulkActionMountToolbarGroup (toolbar placement) and an independent KTL `_ebo` helper group (two constants, an observer Map, a CSS text function, a style injector and preserveBulkEditSelectedRowColors). Nothing here needs a signature change; every item is keep/simplify. The bulk-action classes are wave 3 (port as-is, dead-code and consistency only). The `_ebo` group is wave 2 (modern-ish, KTL-coupled, port with targeted improvements and a shared ensureStyleOnce primitive). Only three real simplifications of substance: a tiny DOM-builder helper to collapse the 120-line ensureModal, a private row-checkbox helper to remove six repeated bulkActionGetSelectableRowCheckboxes(viewElement, this.bulkActionConfig.selection.rowCheckboxClass) calls in the controller, and one shared style injector replacing three identical copies in the file.

Any template rewrite must be byte-identical in class/data attribute output.

The modal lives on document.body with id knack-bulk-basket-<viewId> and survives Knack view re-renders; a new controller instance per render re-adopts it via syncOpenStateFromDom (5119). Moving it inside the view root would make it disappear on every render.
Open state is read from inline style.display (5128), not a class; switching to `hidden` or a class would break syncOpenStateFromDom and consumer CSS.

Buttons come from ktl.fields.addButton (via bulkActionCreateButton 5067) so their markup/classes (kn-button, ktlButtonMargin) are KTL's; do not replace with plain document.createElement('button') or KTL theming is lost.
Close/remove buttons use textContent 'x' with aria-label; unchanged in V2 (any upgrade to an SVG icon is a V3 visual change).
functions.knackPractice: Does not use Knack render events or Knack.views directly; it is pure DOM owned by the controller, and parks the modal outside the .kn-view so Knack re-rendering does not destroy it. That is the correct pattern given Knack replaces view DOM on every render (unverified against live docs). Depends on KTL (ktl.fields.addButton) rather than Knack itself for buttons.
functions.rationale: Already modern (const, optional chaining, dataset, textContent, no jQuery) so the only gain is brevity: ensureModal is 40% of the class and is pure boilerplate that a 10-line element builder removes. Policy puts bulk actions in wave 3 with no signature changes; the public surface (constructor options, eight methods, onX callback fields, modalId) stays identical and no shim is needed. The one genuine bug-smell is the redundant appendChild in renderActions, which is harmless to delete.

functions.name: ktlBulkEditRowColorObservers
functions.currentSignature: const ktlBulkEditRowColorObservers = new Map()  // Map<normalisedViewId, MutationObserver>
modernisations: Keep as a Map keyed by view id. A WeakMap keyed by the <tbody> was considered (auto-GC when Knack replaces the tbody) but preserveBulkEditSelectedRowColors needs to find and disconnect the PREVIOUS observer by view id (5508) before the new tbody exists, which a WeakMap keyed by element cannot do; and changing the global's type would be a signature change.
Trim the three-line comment (5455-5457) to one line; the JSDoc on preserveBulkEditSelectedRowColors already explains replacement-on-render.

If V2 ever moves to a single document-level observer, the per-view disconnect semantics change; keep per-view in wave 2.
functions.knackPractice: Exists precisely because Knack replaces the grid <tbody> on every knack-view-render / knack-records-render, so an observer attached to the old tbody goes stale; keying by view id lets each render swap the observer. Follows the 'never cache elements across renders' rule.

DOM contracts used by CSS and other code: wrapper attributes data-knack-bulk-bar=<viewId>, id bulkActionControlsDiv-<viewId>, classes knackBulkActionBar / ktlFeatureGroup / knackBulkActionButton / knackBulkActionToolbarButton / is-active / is-inactive / is-disabled, button data-bulk-action-key. All must be emitted identically.

Toolbar buttons are created by KTL (ktl.fields.addButton) and may receive KTL's own click handling; adding listeners via addEventListener (6050) rather than onclick is deliberate so KTL handlers are not overwritten.

clearBasket (5787-5793) relies on basketStore.clear() also wiping the stored active action key (verified in createBulkActionBasketStore.clear); if V2 swaps the store, keep that coupling.
functions.knackPractice: Follows the Knack model well: a new controller is built per knack-view-render via mountBulkActionGrid (6733), the view root is resolved fresh each call (resolveViewElement -> bulkActionFindViewRoot -> getViewRootElement, never cached), selection is re-read from the live DOM, and cross-render state lives in sessionStorage (basket store) and in the body-level modal rather than in view DOM. Navigation to the form scene uses bulkActionNavigateToSceneSlug (hash routing) and record ids come from tr#<recordId>, both consistent with Knack's documented conventions (unverified against live docs). It depends on KTL for checkboxes, buttons and the add-ons toolbar div, so it is KTL-coupled rather than Knack-coupled.
functions.rationale: Recent (2026), already ES2020+, no jQuery, well JSDoc'd; policy says port as-is with dead-code and consistency fixes only, and nothing in the 34-method public surface should change, so no shim. The concrete savings are the repeated row-checkbox lookups, the duplicated checked-id computation, the double rebuildRecordMaps, the per-button resolveActiveAction call, hasOwn, and classList.toggle pairs - roughly 130 lines without touching behaviour. Medium risk purely because of size and the number of KTL and sessionStorage interactions; a Playwright test driving a fake grid (checkboxes, master, basket add/remove, runAction with a stub runner) should gate the port.

crossCuttingFindings: Three identical idempotent style injectors exist in the file (ensureBulkActionBaseStyles 5034, ensureBulkEditSelectionStyles 5477, ensureMenuButtonActiveStyles 9505); V2 should ship one ensureStyleOnce(id, css) foundation primitive in wave 1 and make all three thin wrappers. Two of them carry a dead `typeof document === 'undefined'` guard and one does not - inconsistent.

bulkActionFindViewRoot (3689-3693) normalises the view id and then ignores the normalised value, passing the raw viewId to getViewRootElement (6931) which normalises again; it is a pure wrapper and a dedupe candidate already listed in the policy (getViewRootElement vs bulkActionFindViewRoot vs getViewMountElement). preserveBulkEditSelectedRowColors (5503) bypasses both and uses document.getElementById directly - a third way of doing the same thing in one chunk.

File-ordering constraint for V2: BulkActionGridController (5581) uses `bulkActionsApi = KnackBulkActions` as a default parameter, but `const KnackBulkActions` is declared at 6875, and a `globalThis.KnackBulkActions = {...}` merge follows it (6893-6900). With const/TDZ this only works because construction happens after script evaluation; V2 must keep KnackBulkActions (and knackNavigator 797 / knackValueResolver 1787, used at class-body evaluation time in other chunks) declared before anything that may run during script evaluation.

Knack lifecycle events (knack-view-render.any, knack-scene-render) are fired via jQuery .trigger, so ensureBulkActionControllerLifecycleBinding (3660) and every other render binding in the file MUST stay on window.jQuery(document).on(...); a native addEventListener will never receive them. This is the one jQuery dependency V2 cannot remove.

Spelling inconsistency inside the bulk-actions section itself: bulkActionSummarizeRunState / normalizeViewId / preserveBulkEditSelectedRowColors (US) vs bulkActionNormaliseLabelText (UK). All are public globals and cannot be renamed; policy says new identifiers are UK-spelt, so V2 will mix spellings permanently unless UK aliases are added as shims.

KTL coupling is pervasive and undocumented in-repo: ktl.views.addCheckboxesToTable option names, ktl.fields.addButton(parent, label, style, classes, id) positional signature, ktl.views.getKtlAddOnsDiv, the .ktlAddonsDiv / .ktlFeatureGroup / .bulkOpsControlsDiv class contract, and KTL `_ebo` internals (td.bulkEditSelectedRow, data-bulk-edit-saved-bg/color, class bulkEditCb). A short 'KTL contract' comment block (or a tests/fixtures stub of ktl) in V2 would let the bulk-action chunks be tested without KTL.

Timing hacks that should become MutationObserver-based in V3 but are kept in V2 per wave-3 rules: setTimeout(0) re-mount in renderButtonBar (6058-6063) and setTimeout(0) in ensureBulkActionControllerLifecycleBinding (3665).

Global state leaks: bulkActionControllerStore (Map), bulkActionWorkflowRegistry (Set), bulkActionControllerLifecycleBound (let), ktlBulkEditRowColorObservers (Map) are all mutable page globals. Harmless today but if V2 wraps module internals in a block scope these names must still be exposed because they are in eslint/knack-functions-globals.json.

Modal DOM (#knack-bulk-basket-<viewId>) is appended to document.body and never removed; bulkActionSyncControllerVisibility (3641) closes it but leaves the node. One node per bulk-action grid is bounded, but note it for the leak audit.
Line 5181 is mis-indented, confirming no formatter runs on this section; V2 should be formatted by the repo's ESLint config so such drift cannot recur.
